State/local outcomes and vulnerable-group effects remain insufficiently searched.","missing_source_type":"Independent administrative, judicial, or empirical outcome data on implementation, protest treatment, and disparate effects is missing.","official_claim_independence":"E007 is an official action record. The notebook separates inherited January 6 conduct from Biden-period responsibility, but Biden-specific democratic conduct remains thin.","closed_system_silence":"Surveillance, appointment decisions, internal pressure, and informal treatment of dissent may be opaque.","duplicate_reporting":"E005 and E006 overlap in describing Electoral Count Act reform; E006 is legislative-history context, not independent enacted-law evidence.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Reform and democratic safeguards were searched alongside inherited-crisis and civil-society context. Searches for Biden-specific dissent, surveillance, media pressure, and appointments were incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent oversight, court, inspector-general, or investigative evidence on executive treatment of dissent and media is missing.","official_claim_independence":"E005 and E006 are CRS analyses with institutional distance, while E010 is an external country assessment; none directly establishes Biden’s personal treatment of dissent.","open_system_complaint_volume":"High U.S. media and civil-society visibility can amplify partisan complaints and adverse narratives without proving executive responsibility.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"The notebook addresses inherited democratic stress and federal/state election authority, but practical effects across populations and the role of Congress, courts, and state administrators remain underdeveloped.","supporting_evidence_ids":["LF254","LF505","E005","E006","E010"],"unresolved_risks":["Biden-specific treatment of dissent, surveillance, appointments, and media pressure is not established.","The inherited January 6 baseline risks being misread as 2022 conduct."]},"chapter_id":"4B","defensible_evidence_estimate":7,"independent_source_family_estimate":4,"missing_themes":["Treatment of dissent","Surveillance and civil-liberties practice","Media pressure or interference","Appointments and institutional independence","Practical political-equality effects"],"substantive_issues":["Country-level governance indicators are context only.","The enacted reform supports formal responsibility, but Congress materially shaped the result."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E011 is a projection, E012 statutory analysis, and E013 an implementation record; these establish policy and expected mechanisms, not realized economic outcomes or findings of competence.","closed_system_silence":"Internal implementation failures and distributional effects may be obscured by administrative reporting and delayed measurement.","duplicate_reporting":"E011–E013 concern distinct laws and analytic products, but repeated IRA descriptions should not be counted as independent claims.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Policy benefits and implementation architecture were searched. Inflation, household distribution, implementation quality, and correction of mistakes remain explicitly incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent contemporaneous household, distributional, inflation, and implementation-performance evidence is missing.","official_claim_independence":"CBO and CRS provide independent institutional analysis; Commerce provides an official implementation record. Projected benefits remain unverified.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Economic complaints are broad and highly exposed to macroeconomic shocks and partisan attribution, so volume can exaggerate ruler-specific severity.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"National economic indicators are identified as context, but subgroup exposure, inherited inflation conditions, congressional constraints, and external shocks are not fully separated from Biden-attributed policy effects.","supporting_evidence_ids":["LF506","LF719","E011","E012","E013"],"unresolved_risks":["Immediate inflation and household distribution are not adequately evidenced.","Long-term economic outcomes were not observable within the target period."]},"chapter_id":"5B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":4,"missing_themes":["2022 inflation and household burden","Distributional effects","Implementation quality","Policy correction or adaptation","Employment/productivity outcomes attributable to policy"],"substantive_issues":["CBO evidence is projected rather than realized.","National economic outcomes cannot establish ruler competence without a stronger policy and shock attribution analysis."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E007, E009, and E014 establish formal federal actions and implementation steps, not population-wide service findings. The notebook correctly limits PACT evidence to veterans.","closed_system_silence":"Administrative failures, unmet needs, and service-quality problems can remain hidden in agency data and individual case reporting.","duplicate_reporting":"E007 and E009 overlap on public-safety and behavioral-health policy; E014 is distinct but should not be treated as evidence for general-population welfare.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Federal programs and benefits were searched, but adverse searches for affordability, access, regional equity, and durability were incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent service-user, audit, claims, or outcome data on access, quality, and distribution is missing.","official_claim_independence":"E014 uses CRS analysis but relies on statutory and agency implementation records; E007 and E009 are official policy sources without independent outcome checks.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Health and safety complaint volume varies with access to reporting and affected-population visibility; it cannot alone establish national severity.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"The notebook distinguishes veterans from the general population, but subgroup exposure, regional inequity, inherited service conditions, federal/state authority, and pandemic-related shocks remain incompletely addressed.","supporting_evidence_ids":["LF720","LF771","E007","E009","E014"],"unresolved_risks":["General-population service quality and affordability remain unresolved.","Durability and implementation outcomes were not measurable within 2022."]},"chapter_id":"6B","defensible_evidence_estimate":7,"independent_source_family_estimate":4,"missing_themes":["General-population service quality","Regional and subgroup equity","Affordability and access","Independent implementation outcomes","Durability of benefits"],"substantive_issues":["Veterans’ healthcare evidence cannot be generalized to national welfare.","Country-level health, education, and welfare indicators do not establish Biden attribution."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"The notebook explicitly separates disclosure and OGE review from broad integrity claims and reports no independently corroborated 2022 findings of enrichment, deception, obstruction, nepotism, or retaliation.","closed_system_silence":"Personal enrichment, informal influence, obstruction, and retaliation can be concealed through private communications, intermediaries, and limited access to records.","duplicate_reporting":"E015 contains the financial-disclosure release and its conflict-free characterization; the filing fact and the administration’s claim must not be counted as independent evidence.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Favorable disclosure evidence was searched, but adverse and contrary searches for personal enrichment, deception, obstruction, nepotism, and retaliation were not sufficiently developed.","missing_source_type":"Independent investigative, ethics, court, inspector-general, or congressional evidence testing personal-integrity allegations is missing.","official_claim_independence":"OGE certification supports filing review, but the White House statement that there were no conflicts is an official claim requiring independent checks.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Public allegations involving political families and associates are highly amplified and may exaggerate severity without a substantiated finding or nexus to Biden.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Country-level governance indicators and inherited institutional safeguards do not resolve the personal-integrity nexus. It does not make researcher-written scoring or ranking claims.","closed_system_silence":"Administrative implementation problems, internal dissent, and failure to remedy can be difficult to observe during a one-year period.","duplicate_reporting":"Several items are reused across chapters appropriately as global IDs, but overlapping official records must not be counted as independent corroboration.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Policy and implementation evidence was searched. Contrary evidence on failure, adaptation, durability, and long-term results remains incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent performance audits, implementation evaluations, and contemporaneous outcome evidence are missing.","official_claim_independence":"CRS and CBO add independence, but many implementation claims come from official executive-branch records and stated policy mechanisms.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Visible policy controversy and media attention can overstate apparent failure or success without outcome denominators.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"The notebook identifies inherited capacity and federal authority, but does not fully address population exposure, congressional/state constraints, baseline conditions, and external shocks when attributing effectiveness.","supporting_evidence_ids":["LF354","LF820","LF843","E002","E004","E005","E007","E011","E012","E013","E014"],"unresolved_risks":["Long-term outcomes and durability are not yet measurable.","Adaptation and correction after failure are not evidenced.","Local-fact disposition is described but the required explicit audit is absent."]},"chapter_id":"8B","defensible_evidence_estimate":12,"independent_source_family_estimate":6,"missing_themes":["Observable long-term outcomes","Adaptation after failure","Durability","Independent implementation evaluation","Explicit local-data disposition audit"],"substantive_issues":["The chapter spans many policy domains but relies mainly on formal actions and projected mechanisms.","National capacity indicators cannot independently establish Biden’s effectiveness."]}],"global_findings":["All eight selected chapters have material research-recoverable gaps; continuation should cover all selected lenses without expanding scope.","The notebook contains identifiable locators and stable global evidence IDs, but several evidence items bundle multiple claims and official records; deterministic splitting and reconciliation are still required.","Attribution is strongest for formal federal actions and weakest for national outcomes, state/local conduct, and Chapter 7B personal integrity.","Local facts are generally labeled as context rather than ruler evidence, but the required explicit local-data disposition audit is missing.","Favorable and adverse coverage is uneven: policy records are stronger than contrary outcome evidence, independent findings, implementation audits, and personal-attribution evidence.","The 17-locator and 11-source-family counts are QA signals, not saturation findings; the notebook itself identifies recoverable gaps and incomplete searches."],"needs_continuation":true,"reviewer_summary":"Continue the same researcher thread for all eight selected chapters. The dossier has useful official records, CRS/CBO analysis, civil-society assessments, and clearly separated inherited local facts, but it does not yet support a fair evidence handoff on contrary material, implementation outcomes, source independence, or attribution across several domains. Chapter 7B requires the most targeted continuation for independently corroborated personal-integrity evidence; Chapters 1B, 2B, 3B, 4B, 5B, 6B, and 8B also have bounded recoverable gaps in adverse evidence, attribution, outcomes, or missing source types.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":["1B.1","1B.10","1B.2","1B.3","1B.4","1B.5","1B.6","1B.7่?"]}
